messages:
sasha: FYI — ACME reporting repeated p95 spikes and intermittent 429s from their Dedicated pool (pool=dpool-eu2-47). Started ~2023-11-22T10:20Z, p95 jumped from ~60ms to ~2.4s. They see token throttles and some auth retries. Link to customer dashboard: https://console.redwood.example/customer/acme/latency :thinking_face:

jamie: assigning to @rohith and @meera for triage. Can you confirm pool config (MIG layout) and check autoscaler events?

rohith: I'm on it. Quick checks — no autoscaler scale events in the 10:15-10:30 window. Node labels show mixed MIG slices on the same host (3g.20gb and 1g.6gb). Reproduced high SM% bursts on a single physical GPU while other slices look idle. Grabbing NVML/pmc logs now.

meera: Customer sent a repro load pattern that correlates with the spike — concurrent small-model requests. Their repro (they ran from their infra):

```bash
for i in {1..100}; do \\curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H \"Authorization: Bearer $KEY\" -d '{"model":"llm-small","input":"hi","max_tokens":256}' &
done; wait
```

They report ~25% 429s and large p95 jump under that burst.

jamie: thanks. If it's co-residency thrash between MIG slices that's consistent. Short mitigation options: 1) move ACME to a fresh host with homogeneous slices, 2) bump their reserved slots temporarily to reduce co-tenancy, 3) apply a fast canary routing to a slightly larger model variant.

rohith: NVML snapshot (snippet):

```text
[10:20:01] GPU0 SM%: 93, memory.used: 4800MiB, L3_miss: 1.3e6
[10:20:02] GPU1 SM%: 12, memory.used: 1200MiB, L3_miss: 0.12e6
[10:20:03] context-switches spike: 420/sec
```

Shows one slice saturating SM and causing L3 cache thrash; other slices show low utilization but suffer from shared-cache interference.

meera: that aligns with a noisy-slice scenario rather than autoscaler delay. For immediate customer relief I recommend evict-and-reschedule to a homogeneous node and set their pool's min-reserved to 2 slots. Also lower the scale-out threshold temporarily to react faster for this tenant.

sasha: created internal ticket CS-8721 and flagged it P1 for the duration. I've requested the CSM to accept migration. @infra-bot can you start migration action when ready?

infra-bot: scheduled migration started for tenant acme. Evicting pods: acme-gen-5, acme-gen-7 -> rescheduling to ip-10-0-1-45 (homogeneous 3g.20gb slices). ETA ~45s.

jamie: follow-up for runtime team: check kernel selection path and KV-cache pinning for llm-small when run on MIG partitions. If cache policies are too aggressive they exacerbate L3 thrash.

rohith: after migration: p95 back to ~70ms, 0% 429s in the next 2 min window. I'll attach full nvml dump to the ticket and mark repro steps + mitigations.

meera: noted. We'll keep ACME on the reserved host for 24h while we observe. Also adding a perf test to simulate high-concurrency runs against mixed-MIG nodes to capture regressions. :white_check_mark:

sasha: customer notified, CS confirms improved numbers. Closing triage here, will keep CS-8721 open until 24h observation complete. :thumbsup:
